built.D1: The area map pages each surface item of the area's batches (the cases of its site) and reads each published part's display read, at most 4 in flight, at most 256 parts per file. A placed part is drawn at its corners (outline plus content); a not_placed part is counted on the file's line in the placement's own words and never drawn. New parts appear when the batch stream reports a change: the manifest is read again and only parts not yet asked are read.
built.D2: The artifact is fetched through the existing raster-windows artifact route, checked against the display read's bytes and SHA-256, and decoded by a bounded strip TIFF decoder in Studio (no new dependency; deflate through the browser's DecompressionStream). RGB or RGBA as written; one band grey by the part's own min and max, with 'Shaded by this part's own range; heights are not measured.'; nodata, NaN and mask-0 pixels transparent; at most 256 x 256 pixels. Anything else is refused with words and the outline alone is drawn.
built.D3: The point-batches artifact is read as LAS format-6 records (at most 8,192 per part) and drawn as flat points at their placed XY, coloured by Z rank within the part, with 'Coloured by height as written, not measured.'; Z never moves a point.
built.D4: Every line starts 'Display only.'; nothing is written back; parts are never picked. A failed display read, artifact read or decode is named on that file's line and the other parts stay drawn.
built.D5: Decoding runs in one long-lived module worker (surface.worker.ts); the decode time per part is measured in the unit tests on the reader's real windows, since the runtime is not up.

deviation: The task says to refuse compressed TIFFs, but raster_window.py writes every window with deflate (Compression 8). The decoder reads uncompressed and deflate strips and refuses every other compression (for example LZW), tiled layouts, BigTIFF, a predictor and windows over 256 pixels, with words. Refusing deflate would refuse every real part.

realInputs.what: The kept NYC originals (nyc-10013-ortho-2018.tif, nyc-10013-dem-2017.tif and the NYC point cloud) read by the repository's own raster_window.py and point_batch.py, run locally without Docker; the artifacts were written to a scratch folder outside Git and pointed to with ULPIN_SURFACE_WINDOWS.
realInputs.maskCheck: Every transparent pixel count equals the reader's maskedPixels for its window (all 0 on these windows, so the mask path is shown by the test-only fixtures, not by these windows).
realInputs.timingNote: Node 24 on the main test thread, machine shared with other runs; in the browser the same code runs in the worker, off the frame. No frame time was measured.

gaps: No runtime, browser or frame measurement: decode time is per part in unit tests only.
Points are placed bilinearly from the batch's native XY extent to its placed corners; across the projection change this is approximate, for display only.
A display read that fails (for example a part read before the area existed) is named on the line and asked again only at the next page of that file; there is no timed retry.
Each file's line is shown as the hint of its switch in the layer list (and in a small key on the windowed area).
notRun: No Docker, runtime, GPU or provider call. The UI was not opened in a browser; Studio changes are for review by hand.
